claim: Dropping the returned scalar phase cannot change the full controlled operation.
reason: The full unitary is verified with alpha=0.493, beta=0.6310000000000001, gamma=1.1730000000000003, delta=-0.28300000000000003. Chronological native calls are rz(delta),ry(gamma),rz(beta). Nine actual circuits verify direct, native and coherent-control cases. In basis 00,01,10,11 with qubit 0 control and qubit 1 target, C(U)=diag(I,U). Controlled native V requires actual phase(0,theta=alpha) after C(V). Dropping alpha changes the full operation: raw Frobenius difference is about 0.6901680590, and the difference remains nonzero even after aligning one phase for the whole controlled operator. Computational-basis probabilities happen to agree here but full complex outputs differ. A control-branch phase repair restores the operator; a scalar on the entire output does not. The supplied omission claim is refuted for this concrete unitary.
